model_annotation: The figure contains two stacked bar charts that illustrate annual values expressed as “% des BIP” for three government levels—Bund (blue), Länder (purple), and Gemeinden (green)—with a black line labeled “Gebietskörperschaften insgesamt” showing the total across the stacked components; both panels share the same time axis and include a vertical dashed reference line around the year 2000 annotated with an arrow and the label “Bahnreform.” In each panel, the horizontal axis lists years from 1991 to 2023 (shown with rotated labels at intervals), and the vertical axis is labeled “% des BIP¹” on a linear scale ranging from about −0.5 to 3.5 with regularly spaced tick marks at 0.5-unit intervals. In the left panel, each year is represented by a stacked column whose total height generally lies between roughly 2.2 and 3.3% of GDP, with the black total line tracking the top of the stacks; the blue Bund segment is typically around ~0.6–1.1, the purple Länder segment around ~0.6–0.9, and the green Gemeinden segment around ~0.7–1.7, with the tallest totals appearing in the early 1990s (just above ~3.0) and again near the early 2020s (around ~3.0), and lower totals around the mid-2000s (near ~2.2–2.4). In the right panel, the same stacked color scheme is used but the annual totals are much closer to zero, with stacks and the black total line fluctuating roughly between about −0.2 and +0.8; early years (around 1991–1994) show a prominent positive green Gemeinden contribution (bringing totals near ~0.7–0.8), while many later years show small positive and negative contributions across the three colors, including periods where the green segment dips below zero and the total line approaches or slightly crosses zero, and a visible positive bump near the early 2020s where the total line rises to roughly ~0.4–0.5 before returning toward ~0.0 by 2023. The bars are arranged chronologically by year (not sorted by magnitude), and no individual bars appear specially highlighted beyond the consistent color coding, the overlaid black total line, and the dashed vertical reference line marking the reform point.
